source.title: A Function Centric Perspective On Flat and Sharp Minima
source.authors: Israel Mason-Williams; Gabryel Mason-Williams; H. Yannakoudakis

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper’s full text, including appendices. It states publication in Transactions on Machine Learning Research (10/2026), later than the supplied arXiv year.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures several sharpness metrics alongside generalization gaps and compares them across training controls and tasks. Its sharpness measures and experiments differ from V7’s magnitude-scaled perturbation measure and matched low-training-loss comparison.
record.gate_note: Own results on sharpness and generalization gaps bear on V7’s broad relationship, but the study does not use V7’s specific magnitude-aware perturbation measure. Table values and explicit textual comparisons are included; cited findings from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: The random-label experiment tests V1's coexistence of memorization capacity and natural-label generalization using ResNet18. The fixed-epoch batch-size comparisons also bear on V5. The sharpness experiments measure different quantities from V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and do not directly test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: under the measures and settings studied, sharpness is not a universal indicator of poor generalization; its interpretation depends on the learned function, model inductive bias and training controls. The authors explicitly leave the causal relationship unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Studies sharpness and generalization under matched-seed regularization controls, synthetic decision-boundary changes, and randomized labels; it does not reproduce V7’s magnitude-aware perturbation measure or comparison protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: The relationship varies with training control, dataset, architecture, learning rate, batch size, and SAM ρ. TinyImageNet Relative Flatness could not be computed; sharpness rankings and generalization outcomes vary across settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Across several regularization controls, smaller generalization gaps coincide with higher Fisher-Rao norm, Relative Flatness and average-case SAM-Sharpness; SAM alone on TinyImageNet provides a contrasting direction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Associations between these particular geometry measures and generalization gaps depend on training controls and settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Tightening make_circles class boundaries increases Fisher-Rao norm and Relative Flatness while training and test accuracy remain 100%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These geometry measures can increase with tighter class boundaries despite perfect generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing CIFAR10 label randomization increases Fisher-Rao norm and Relative Flatness measured on unaltered training data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fitting increasingly randomized labels can increase these geometry measures.

record.peer_reviewed: Transactions on Machine Learning Research (10/2026), as stated in the supplied text
record.problems: The study does not resolve causality. Its specific results do not use V7’s magnitude-aware perturbation metric. TinyImageNet Relative Flatness is unavailable; some results are figure-only. The text reports means ± SEM over ten seeds for the high-dimensional controls.
record.rows_left_out: Numerous additional architecture–dataset–control combinations and hyperparameter sweeps report sharpness and generalization metrics, including Tables 6, 20–47 and Appendix H. They are omitted to keep the extraction focused; the main CIFAR10 ResNet18 comparison, a TinyImageNet contrast, the stated SAM-radius setting, and the randomized-label result are retained. Figure-only test-accuracy values for the randomized-label experiment are not transcribed.

untested.parts: The original architectures and ImageNet setting are not reproduced. Chance-level held-out accuracy with fully randomized labels cannot be verified numerically from the supplied figure transcription.
No width sweep through and beyond interpolation.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparison.
No broad batch-size sweep locating a workload-dependent threshold, or experiments with longer training, learning-rate scaling, warmup, or normalization changes to recover performance.

No magnitude-aware perturbation-tolerance measurement or ranking against norm- and margin-based alternatives under the specified comparison protocol. Fisher-Rao norm, Relative Flatness and average-case SAM-Sharpness are different measures.
No removal of highly memorized examples followed by retraining.

missing.what: Add the natural-label held-out performance to the V1 comparison: Table 13 gives 100% natural-label training accuracy, and the matching baseline recipe in Table 3 gives test accuracy 0.720 ±0.002.

Add direct fixed-epoch batch-size comparison rows for ResNet18 and VGG19 at each learning rate. The component tables are declared omitted in rows_left_out, but the current rows cannot carry the V5 verdict.

record.verdict_notes: Do not transfer conclusions about the study's sharpness metrics to V7's specific magnitude-aware measure. Smaller gaps can also reflect reduced training accuracy, particularly with augmentation on TinyImageNet and large SAM radii. The 2025 arXiv identifier and October 2026 version/publication date are compatible.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the same architectures and training recipes fitting random labels and natural labels as specified.
Does not sweep network width past the interpolation threshold.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected architectures for image generalization.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD.
Does not test large-batch generalization penalties against smaller batches under fixed epoch budgets.

Tests relationships between generalization gap and Fisher-Rao norm, Relative Flatness, and SAM-Sharpness, but does not test the specified magnitude-aware perturbation measure or rank it against norm- and margin-based measures.
Does not remove memorized examples and retrain.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Training on CIFAR10 with increasing randomized training labels; measured sharpness and test accuracy.
rows.measure: Fisher-Rao norm and Relative Flatness rise as randomized data percentage increases; Table 13 reports Fisher-Rao norm 0.031 ±0.001 at 0% and 283.181 ±0.129 at 100%, and Relative Flatness 33.700 ±0.949 at 0% and 47.095 ±0.543 at 100%.
rows.value: At 100% randomized: train accuracy 1.000 ±0.000; train loss 1.094E-04 ±1.490E − 06; test accuracy shown in Figure 10 only.
rows.uncertainty: ± values as stated for tabulated metrics
rows.note: Training labels are randomized, so this does not establish the claimed same-distribution natural-label generalization relationship.
rows.check: Relink to V1: Table 13 reports perfect training accuracy for both natural and fully randomized labels under the same recipe. Natural-label held-out accuracy is far above chance. The extracted figure text does not permit a reliable numerical reading of fully randomized-label test accuracy, so that component remains undetermined. Sharpness is evaluated on unaltered training data, whereas training accuracy concerns the labels used for fitting.
